cities.name: Chicago

photo.alt: Chicago skyline at sunrise seen across Lake Michigan

funFacts: Chicago averages 38.4 inches of snow a year, so booties season runs from roughly December through March, and the sidewalk salt that comes with it is its own paw hazard.

Lake Michigan works like a giant radiator in reverse: lakefront walks often run 5 to 10 degrees cooler than inland blocks on hot summer afternoons, which makes the 26 miles of lakefront trail a smart July route.
Montrose Dog Beach in Uptown is one of the largest off-leash dog beaches in the country, and on a warm day the water is the best cooldown in the city.

Despite the nickname, the Windy City isn't unusually windy. Its average wind speed of about 10 mph ranks behind Boston and Oklahoma City. Most historians trace the name to 19th-century politics, not weather.

Chicago's temperature swing is real: the city has officially hit 105 degrees and negative 27 degrees, a 132-degree spread, so a Chicago pet wardrobe genuinely needs both a cooling vest and a winter coat.

source.name: NOAA 1991–2020 U.S. Climate Normals, Chicago O'Hare (NWS Chicago)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Chicago?
faq.a: Chicago's July average high is 84.5 degrees, which already sits in the risky band for most dogs. On days above about 82 degrees, keep outings to short potty breaks in early morning or late evening, and check pavement with the 7-second test, since asphalt on a Chicago summer afternoon can run 40 to 60 degrees hotter than the air.

faq.q: Does my dog need a winter coat in Chicago?
faq.a: For most dogs, yes for part of the year. Chicago's January average high is only 31.6 degrees with an average low of 18.8, and the city averages 38.4 inches of snow. Small, short-coated, senior, and lean dogs benefit from a coat below about 45 degrees, and most dogs need protection in the 20-to-32-degree range.

faq.q: What's the best time of day to walk a dog in Chicago in summer?
faq.a: Early morning is best, before pavement heats up, with late evening second. Chicago's lakefront also runs 5 to 10 degrees cooler than inland streets on hot afternoons, so a shaded lakefront route buys you extra safe minutes when the day warms.

funFacts: Central Park's average July high is 84.9F, already past the 82F risky range for dog walks, so summer strolls are safest before 9 am.

January lows average 27.9F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band, which means small and senior dogs should wear coats from roughly November through March.
The city has swung from a record 106F (July 9, 1936) to -15F (February 9, 1934), so a New York pet wardrobe genuinely needs both cooling and insulation.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in New York City?
faq.a: Use caution above 77F, treat 82F as risky, and skip midday walks at 90F and up. New York's average July high is 84.9F, so in July and August aim for early morning or after sunset, and remember that humidity makes heat feel worse. Asphalt also holds heat long after the air cools.

faq.q: Does my dog need a winter coat in New York?
faq.a: Small, senior, and short-coated dogs need coats below 45F, and New York's average highs stay at or below 44.3F from December through March. With January lows averaging 27.9F, add booties or paw balm to protect pads from ice-melt salt.

faq.q: How does snow in New York affect dog walks?
faq.a: The city averages 29.8 inches of snow a year, peaking at 10.1 inches in February. Snowbanks hide debris and rock salt burns paws, so rinse feet after walks and keep outings short when temperatures sit in the 20 to 32F caution band.

cities.name: Los Angeles

photo.alt: Downtown Los Angeles skyline with mountains in the distance

funFacts: Downtown LA's average high peaks at 84.0F in August, right at the edge of risky for dog walks, so late-summer mornings beat afternoon pavement.
Los Angeles records no measurable snow in its climate normals, and even January highs average 68.0F, so most dogs never need a winter coat here.
LA hit 113F on September 27, 2010, a reminder that fall heat waves, not just summer ones, can make sidewalks dangerous for paws.
July and August average almost no rain (0.02 and 0.00 inches), so dry-season trails get dusty: carry water for your dog on every hike.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Los Angeles?
faq.a: Use caution above 77F, treat 82F as risky, and skip walks at 90F and up. Downtown LA averages 82.0F in July and 84.0F in August, so summer midday walks are borderline by default: stick to mornings, shade, and grass instead of asphalt.

faq.q: Do dogs need coats in Los Angeles?
faq.a: Rarely. Even January averages a 68.0F high and a 48.9F low, so only small, senior, or very short-coated dogs will want a light layer on the occasional early morning that dips below 45F.

faq.q: Are fall heat waves in Los Angeles a risk for pets?
faq.a: Yes. September is LA's third-hottest month at an 83.0F average high, and the all-time record of 113F came on September 27, 2010. Keep the 90F no-walk rule in mind through October and test pavement with your palm before any afternoon outing.

cities.name: Houston

photo.alt: Downtown Houston skyline viewed from the west over Buffalo Bayou

funFacts: Houston's average highs run 91.0F to 93.5F from June through August, past the 90F danger line for dog walks, so summer exercise belongs at dawn.
Nights barely cool off in a Houston summer: July and August lows average 76.6F and 76.7F, so humid evenings often stay in the caution zone and indoor play beats evening fetch.
Houston's climate normals show no measurable annual snowfall, yet the city has dropped to 5F (January 18, 1930), so keep one dog coat on hand for rare Arctic blasts.
With June averaging 6.09 inches of rain and most months topping 4 inches, Houston dogs need a towel routine and paw checks after soggy walks.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Houston?
faq.a: Houston's average high is at or above 91.0F from June through August, beyond the 90F danger threshold, so walk at dawn when temperatures are closest to the 76.6F average low. Humidity makes it worse: caution starts at 77F here, and midday summer walks should simply be skipped.

faq.q: Why does Houston humidity matter so much for dogs?
faq.a: Dogs cool themselves by panting, and humid air slows that down, so a humid 85F Houston day can stress a dog like a much hotter dry day. With summer lows averaging near 76.7F, even evenings hover at the 77F caution line: choose dawn walks and carry water.

faq.q: How does Houston rain affect dog routines?
faq.a: Houston averages more than 4 inches of rain in eight months of the year, with June the wettest at 6.09 inches. Flash flooding is the real hazard: avoid bayou trails during storms, dry ears and paws after wet walks, and keep indoor enrichment ready for stormy days.

cities.name: Phoenix

photo.alt: Downtown Phoenix skyline seen from South Mountain during the day

funFacts: Phoenix's average June high is 104.2F and July's is 106.5F, far past the 90F danger line, so summer dog walks are dawn-only, full stop.
Even overnight offers little relief: July lows average 84.5F, which is already above the 82F risky threshold before the sun comes up.
Phoenix hit 122F on June 26, 1990, and on days anywhere near that, asphalt can blister paw pads in seconds: always do the seven-second back-of-hand pavement test.
The flip side of desert life: December through February highs average 66.2F to 70.8F, making Phoenix winters some of the best dog-walking weather in the country.

source.name: NOAA 1991-2020 U.S. Climate Normals (Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Phoenix?
faq.a: From May (94.5F average high) through September (100.4F), Phoenix afternoons are past the 90F danger threshold, so walk at dawn only. In July even the average low is 84.5F, above the 82F risky line, so keep summer outings short, shaded, and on grass.

faq.q: How hot does Phoenix pavement get for paws?
faq.a: Pavement can run 40 to 60 degrees hotter than the air, and Phoenix averages a 106.5F air temperature in July. If you cannot hold the back of your hand on the asphalt for seven seconds, it is too hot for paws: use booties, walk on grass, or wait for dawn.

faq.q: Is winter in Phoenix good for dogs?
faq.a: Yes. December and January highs average 66.2F and 67.6F with lows in the mid 40s, ideal walking weather. Only very small or senior dogs need a light coat on mornings that dip below the 45F coat threshold.

The city averages 23.1 inches of snow a year, peaking at 8.4 inches in February, so plan for salted sidewalks and post-walk paw rinses all winter.
January lows average 26.0F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band, which means coats for small and senior dogs and shorter walks in deep winter.
Philadelphia's extremes run from 106F (August 7, 1918) to -11F (February 9, 1934), one of the widest pet-comfort ranges on the East Coast.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Philadelphia?
faq.a: Use caution above 77F, treat 82F as risky, and skip walks at 90F and up. Philadelphia averages 87.8F in July and 85.8F in August, so summer walks belong in the early morning, and river-valley humidity makes those numbers feel even hotter.

faq.q: Does my dog need a winter coat in Philadelphia?
faq.a: Small, senior, and thin-coated dogs need coats below 45F, and Philadelphia's average highs sit at or below 46.0F from December through February. With January lows averaging 26.0F, limit late-night walks and watch for shivering or paw-lifting.

faq.q: How does Philadelphia snow affect dog walks?
faq.a: Philadelphia averages 23.1 inches of snow a season, with February the snowiest at 8.4 inches. Rock salt is the biggest hazard: wipe paws after every walk, use pet-safe ice melt at home, and keep walks brief when temperatures fall into the 20 to 32F caution band.

cities.name: San Antonio

photo.alt: Downtown San Antonio skyline on a clear day

From June through September, average lows sit between 69.6F and 74.9F, so even late evenings often land in the above-77F caution zone once humidity is factored in.
The city has seen both 111F (September 5, 2000) and 0F (January 31, 1949), so a light dog coat is worth owning even in South Texas.
San Antonio averages just 0.2 inches of snow a year, so the paw hazards here are hot pavement and summer asphalt, not ice melt.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in San Antonio?
faq.a: San Antonio's average highs run 92.4F to 96.0F from June through August, past the 90F danger threshold, so walk at dawn and skip midday entirely. May (86.6F) and September (90.1F) also call for the 77F caution and 82F risky rules.

faq.q: Do dogs need winter gear in San Antonio?
faq.a: Mostly no, but January lows average 41.0F, below the 45F coat threshold for small and senior dogs, and the city once dropped to 0F on January 31, 1949. A light sweater for cold snaps covers it.

faq.q: When does San Antonio weather force indoor days for pets?
faq.a: Summer afternoons are the main trigger, with June through August highs averaging 92.4F to 96.0F. May is also the wettest month at 4.40 inches of rain, so keep puzzle toys and indoor games ready for thunderstorm days.

cities.name: San Diego

photo.alt: San Diego skyline at dawn seen from Coronado Island across the bay

funFacts: San Diego's warmest month, August, averages just a 77.3F high, meaning most of the year sits at or below the 77F caution line: arguably the best dog-walking climate of any big US city.
January averages a 66.4F high and a 50.3F low, so even midwinter walks rarely call for a dog coat.
Extremes still happen: San Diego hit 111F on September 26, 1963, so watch for fall Santa Ana heat spikes before afternoon beach runs.
With no measurable snow in its normals and only about 9.8 inches of rain a year, mostly December through March, true indoor days are rare for San Diego pets.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in San Diego?
faq.a: Rarely, by the averages: even August, the warmest month, averages 77.3F, right at the 77F caution line. On unusual days apply the standard rules, cautious above 77F, risky above 82F, and skip walks at 90F and up, which mostly happens during Santa Ana events.

faq.q: What are Santa Ana heat spikes and do they affect dogs?
faq.a: September averages a 77.2F high but holds the all-time record of 111F (September 26, 1963), so fall Santa Ana winds are the one time San Diego dogs face real heat risk. On those days walk early, carry water, and palm-test the pavement.

faq.q: Do dogs need coats in San Diego?
faq.a: Almost never: January, the coolest month, averages a 66.4F high and a 50.3F low, above the 45F coat threshold. Only tiny, senior, or freshly groomed dogs may want a light layer on damp winter mornings near 50F.

cities.name: Dallas

Dallas averages only 1.7 inches of snow a year, mostly in February (0.9 inches), so ice storms rather than snow drifts are the paw hazard to watch.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Dallas?
faq.a: From June through August, Dallas average highs run 92.7F to 97.1F, past the 90F danger threshold, so walk at dawn and never on afternoon asphalt. July lows still average 77.7F, so even early walks call for water and shade, and the 77F caution rule applies May through September.

faq.q: How cold does Dallas get for dogs in winter?
faq.a: January lows average 37.9F, below the 45F coat threshold for small and senior dogs, and Arctic fronts have driven the area to -10F (February 12, 1899). Most winter afternoons, with highs near 57.7F, are prime walking weather.

faq.q: What about Dallas thunderstorms and rain?
faq.a: October is Dallas's wettest month at 4.79 inches, with May close behind at 4.57 inches, and both peak seasons bring severe thunderstorms. Keep a storm-anxiety plan for your pet (interior room, white noise) and dry paws after wet walks.

cities.name: Austin

photo.alt: Aerial view of the Austin skyline along the Colorado River

funFacts: Austin's average high reaches 97.8F in August, the hottest month, so dawn walks and shaded lake trails are the summer routine for dogs here.
August lows average 75.1F, so even pre-dawn summer walks start near the 77F caution line: bring water every single time.
Camp Mabry has recorded 112F (September 5, 2000, and August 28, 2011) and -2F (January 31, 1949), so Austin pets need a heat plan and at least one decent coat.
Austin averages just 0.2 inches of snow a year, while May brings 5.04 inches of rain, the wettest month, so storm comfort matters far more than snow gear.

source.name: NOAA 1991-2020 U.S. Climate Normals (Camp Mabry)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Austin?
faq.a: June through August average highs run 93.2F to 97.8F, past the 90F danger threshold, so walk at dawn when temperatures are nearest the 72.9F to 75.1F summer lows. In spring and fall use the 77F caution and 82F risky rules, and always palm-test the pavement.

faq.q: How do Austin's spring storms affect dogs?
faq.a: May is Austin's wettest month at 5.04 inches of rain, much of it from intense thunderstorms. Plan indoor enrichment for storm afternoons, keep ID tags current in case a scared pet bolts, and towel off paws after soggy trail walks.

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in Austin?
faq.a: January lows average 41.8F, under the 45F coat threshold for small and senior dogs, though highs recover to 62.5F most afternoons. Hard freezes do happen (the record is -2F on January 31, 1949), so bring pets indoors during Arctic fronts.

cities.name: Jacksonville

Summer is storm season: June through September each average 6.77 to 7.60 inches of rain, so plan indoor games around the near-daily thunderstorm hours.
Even in January, highs average 65.5F, great walking weather, though lows of 42.4F mean thin-coated dogs may want a light sweater at dawn.
Jacksonville's normals show no measurable snow, but the city fell to 7F on January 21, 1985, proof that Florida pets can still meet a hard freeze.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Jacksonville?
faq.a: July averages 91.9F, above the 90F danger threshold, and coastal humidity makes it feel worse, so summer walks belong at dawn when lows average 72.7F. From May through September apply the 77F caution and 82F risky rules.

faq.q: How does Jacksonville humidity affect dogs?
faq.a: Humid air slows a dog's panting-based cooling, so an 85F Jacksonville afternoon can stress a dog like a much hotter dry day. With September still averaging an 87.1F high, keep the early-walk habit going well into fall.

faq.q: What about Jacksonville's rainy season?
faq.a: June is the wettest month at 7.60 inches, and September is close behind at 7.56 inches. Afternoon thunderstorms are near-daily in summer, so schedule walks for mornings, watch for lightning at the beach, and towel dogs off to prevent hot spots.

cities.name: Auckland

photo.alt: Auckland skyline and Sky Tower seen across the harbour from Devonport

funFacts: Auckland's marine climate is remarkably dog friendly: average highs span only 58.3F in July to 75.9F in February, so most days of the year fall inside the safe walking zone.

Even at its most extreme, Auckland Airport has never recorded higher than 86.9F, below the 90F danger line, but dark asphalt and the region's black-sand west coast beaches can still get uncomfortably hot for paws on sunny February afternoons.
Auckland sits on a narrow isthmus between the Waitemata and Manukau harbours, so a cooling sea breeze is rarely far away on warm-season walks.
Winters are mild and wet rather than snowy: July lows average 45.9F, right at the coat threshold for small and senior dogs, and snow essentially never falls in the city.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Auckland?
faq.a: Rarely, by world standards: February, the warmest month, averages a 75.9F high, just under the 77F caution band. On the occasional sunny day that pushes past 77F, shift walks to the morning, offer water, and test dark pavement or black sand with the back of your hand before letting paws on it.

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in Auckland's winter?
faq.a: Small, senior, and thin-coated dogs often do: July and August lows average 45.9F and 46.9F, right around the 45F coat threshold, and wind plus rain makes it feel colder. Healthy double-coated breeds are generally fine year round.

faq.q: How does Auckland weather change dog walking through the year?
faq.a: Temperature is rarely the problem, rain is: the record low at Auckland Airport is only 25.0F, so hard freezes are exceptional. Plan around winter showers, towel your dog off after wet walks when lows sit near 45.9F, and enjoy the long safe-walking season the 58.3F to 75.9F range of average highs provides.

cities.name: Tokyo

Despite the hot summers, Tokyo averages only about 3.1 inches of snow a year, nearly all in January and February, so most city dogs never need serious snow gear.
January highs average 49.6F with lows of 34.2F: brisk but very walkable, making winter the season for the long park walks that humid summer rules out.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Tokyo?
faq.a: From late June through mid September. July and August average highs of 85.8F and 88.3F, well past the 82F risky band, and Tokyo's humidity makes it feel worse. Walk at dawn, keep midday outings to a few minutes, and press the back of your hand to the asphalt before every summer walk.

faq.q: Does it snow enough in Tokyo to bother my dog?
faq.a: Rarely: the yearly average is about 3.1 inches, almost all in January and February. The bigger winter consideration is the 34.2F average January low, so put a coat on small or senior dogs once temperatures drop below 45F.

faq.q: How should I handle Tokyo's rainy season with a dog?
faq.a: June's tsuyu rains arrive with average highs of 79.0F and lows of 65.3F, and the humidity pushes the heat stress of a 79F day toward the 82F risky band. Favor early-morning walks between showers and dry your dog's paws and coat afterward to prevent skin problems.

cities.name: Osaka

funFacts: Osaka is one of Japan's hottest big cities: August averages a 92.7F high, past the 90F dangerous line, and lows of 78.4F keep nights tropical for panting dogs.
Osaka's record high of 102.4F (observations since 1883) means summer midday asphalt can scorch paws; riverside dawn walks are the local summer default.
Snow is nearly a non-event: Osaka averages only about 0.4 inches a year, so winter gear is about the 37.4F January lows, not snowdrifts.
Spring and autumn are the sweet spots: April highs average 67.8F and November 64.0F, ideal weather for long loops around the Osaka Castle moats.

source.name: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) 1991-2020 normals (Osaka)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Osaka?
faq.a: Mid June through mid September. August averages a 92.7F high, beyond the 90F dangerous threshold, and July's 89.2F is firmly in risky territory. Walk at dawn, carry water, and skip midday outings entirely in high summer.

faq.q: How cold do Osaka winters get for dogs?
faq.a: Mild by Japanese standards: January averages a 49.5F high and a 37.4F low. Small, senior, and short-haired dogs should wear a coat once it drops below 45F, which covers most winter mornings, but the record low of 18.5F shows true cold snaps are rare.

faq.q: Does Osaka's rainy season affect dog walks?
faq.a: June's rains come with average highs of 82.4F, already past the 82F risky band before humidity is counted, so muggy rainy-season days deserve the same caution as midsummer. Aim for early walks and dry paws thoroughly afterward.

cities.name: Seoul

photo.alt: Seoul skyline along the Han River

funFacts: Seoul swings roughly 50 degrees between seasons: January highs average just 35.8F while August reaches 86.0F, so dogs here need both a winter coat plan and a summer heat plan.
January lows average 22.1F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band, and the record low of -9.6F (observations since 1907) means wind chill can push walks into dangerous territory fast.
Seoul averages about 24 snow days a year, roughly 7 of them in January alone, so road salt rinses and paw checks are standard winter routine.

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Seoul?
faq.a: January lows average 22.1F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band, and anything below 20F is dangerous for most dogs. Keep December through February walks short, coat small and senior dogs whenever it is below 45F, and watch for ice on sidewalks.

faq.q: Is summer in Seoul risky for dogs too?
faq.a: Yes. August averages a 86.0F high, past the 82F risky band, the record is 103.3F, and June to July monsoon humidity makes it feel hotter still. Shift to dawn walks and keep flat-faced breeds indoors on the muggiest afternoons.

faq.q: How should I handle snow and salt on Seoul walks?
faq.a: Seoul averages about 24 snow days a year, with roughly 7 in January, and sidewalks get salted heavily. Rinse or wipe paws after every winter walk, consider booties for long outings, and remember January's 35.8F average high means snow often lingers.

cities.name: Singapore

photo.alt: Singapore's Marina Bay skyline seen from Marina Bay Sands

funFacts: Singapore has no real seasons: average highs sit between 86.9F and 90.3F every single month, so heat management is a 365-day job for dog owners.
Overnight lows never leave the mid 70s (75.7F to 78.3F), which means even pre-dawn walks are warm; shade, water, and short loops matter more than clever timing.
The all-time record low is just 66.9F, so a Singapore dog will never need a winter coat, ever.
Sitting about one degree north of the equator, Singapore pairs its 88.5F afternoons with tropical humidity that pushes effective heat stress well past the 90F danger line.

source.name: Meteorological Service Singapore / National Environment Agency 1991-2020 normals

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Singapore?
faq.a: Most afternoons, all year: every month averages highs between 86.9F and 90.3F, past the 82F risky band, and humidity makes it feel worse. Walk before 8 am or after sunset, keep loops short and shaded, and always carry water.

faq.q: Does Singapore's humidity really matter for dogs?
faq.a: Enormously. Nights only cool to about 75.7F to 78.3F, so dogs never get a low-humidity recovery window, and panting works poorly in saturated air. Flat-faced breeds are at risk even at the 87.1F January average high, so treat air conditioning as part of their care.

faq.q: How do the monsoon seasons change dog walking in Singapore?
faq.a: They change the rain, not the heat: even December, the coolest month, still averages an 86.9F high, and the record low is only 66.9F. Use the cloud cover and post-shower cooling to your advantage, but keep paws dried and skin folds clean to prevent hot spots in the constant humidity.

cities.name: Hong Kong

photo.alt: Hong Kong Island skyline across Victoria Harbour

funFacts: Hong Kong summers are long and sticky: June through August average highs of 87.3F to 88.9F with lows above 79F, and sea humidity pushes conditions past the 90F danger line on many afternoons.
The Hong Kong Observatory's record low is exactly 32.0F, set on January 18, 1893, so icy paws are a historical footnote here while heat is the everyday concern.
Hong Kong's famously steep streets and hill trails add exertion heat: even October, with an average high of 82.6F, calls for water breaks on uphill dog hikes.
Winter is the walking jackpot: January averages a 65.7F high and a 58.3F low, comfortable for nearly any breed at any hour of the day.

source.name: Hong Kong Observatory 1991-2020 normals

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Hong Kong?
faq.a: May through September. July averages an 88.9F high, well past the 82F risky band, the record is 97.9F, and humidity off the South China Sea makes every degree feel worse. Walk at dawn, choose shaded harbourfront routes over exposed hill climbs, and carry water.

faq.q: How does typhoon season affect dog owners in Hong Kong?
faq.a: Typhoon season peaks July through September, exactly when average lows still sit near 80.4F. Between storms the air is at its most humid, so keep walks short, and during typhoon signals keep dogs indoors with enrichment games rather than risking flying debris outside.

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in a Hong Kong winter?
faq.a: Almost never: January lows average 58.3F, far above the 45F coat threshold. Only tiny, elderly, or clipped dogs might want a light layer during a rare cold surge, and even the all-time record low is just 32.0F.

cities.name: Bangkok

photo.alt: High-rise skyline of Bangkok's Sukhumvit district

funFacts: Bangkok's 'cool' season is not cool: December, the mildest month, still averages a 90.1F high, sitting right at the 90F dangerous line for dog walks.

Nights offer little relief: average lows range from 73.8F to 81.0F year round, so pavement stays warm even before sunrise.
Monsoon rains from roughly May through October shave a few degrees off the highs (91.9F in August versus 96.3F in April) but repay it with humidity that keeps heat stress high for dogs.

source.name: NOAA WMO 1991-2020 Climate Normals (Bangkok Metropolis) / Thai Meteorological Department extremes

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Bangkok?
faq.a: Essentially every midday, all year: monthly average highs run from 90.1F to 96.3F, at or above the 90F dangerous threshold, and humidity compounds it. Walk before sunrise or well after dark, favor grass and soi shade over asphalt, and keep sessions short in April and May.

faq.q: How does the monsoon season change dog care in Bangkok?
faq.a: From May to October, rain cools highs slightly (August averages 91.9F) but floods streets and spikes humidity. Avoid letting dogs wade in floodwater, dry paws and belly after wet walks, and use covered or indoor exercise when downpours hit.

faq.q: Does Bangkok ever get cold enough to worry a dog?
faq.a: No. The all-time record low is 49.8F, from January 1955, and typical December lows average 73.8F. No coat is ever needed; the entire care plan here is heat, hydration, and paw protection.

cities.name: Dubai

Winter is the payoff season: January averages a 75.0F high and a 57.7F low, some of the best dog-walking weather anywhere.
Humidity rolling in off the Gulf makes late-summer 102.0F September afternoons feel even hotter, so flat-faced breeds should simply stay in air conditioning until October.

source.name: NOAA WMO 1991-2020 Climate Normals (Dubai International Airport)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Dubai?
faq.a: June through September is dangerous at almost any daylight hour: average highs run 103.6F to 106.3F, far past the 90F dangerous threshold. Walk briefly at dawn, use booties or grass routes because sand and asphalt hold heat, and carry water every time.

faq.q: Is winter in Dubai safe for dog walks?
faq.a: Yes, it is the best season: January averages a 75.0F high, under the 77F caution band, with pleasant 57.7F nights. November through March is when Dubai dogs can take long daytime walks and beach outings.

faq.q: Will my dog ever need a coat in Dubai?
faq.a: Practically never: the lowest temperature in the 1991-2020 record is 45.3F, right at the small-dog coat threshold, and typical January lows are 57.7F. Skip the wardrobe and invest in cooling mats, water bowls, and paw protection instead.

cities.name: Stockholm

January and February lows average 26.8F and 26.2F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band where walk length should shrink and small dogs need serious coats.
The record low of -18.8F (observations since 1901) is far below the 20F danger line, so on true cold snaps even husky-types should keep outings brief.

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Stockholm?
faq.a: January lows average 26.8F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band, so keep midwinter walks shorter and watch paws for ice balls. Below 20F, which the record -18.8F shows is possible, limit outings to quick relief breaks for all but the hardiest breeds.

faq.q: How should I manage snow season for my dog in Stockholm?
faq.a: Expect about 40.4 inches of snow a year, peaking near 10.1 inches in February. Rinse road salt and gravel grit off paws after every walk, trim fur between pads to reduce ice buildup, and consider booties for long outings.

faq.q: Do Stockholm summers ever get too hot for dogs?
faq.a: Rarely: July averages a 74.5F high, under the 77F caution band, so most summer days are ideal. During an occasional heat wave (the record is 95.7F), shift walks to the long, bright mornings and evenings and offer swimming spots along the waterfront.

cities.name: Copenhagen

Since records began in 1768, Copenhagen has ranged from 96.1F down to -17.7F, yet a typical July peaks at just a 72.9F average high, below the 77F caution line.
Wind off the Oresund strait makes 33.3F January nights feel colder than the thermometer reads, so a windproof dog coat beats a merely thick one here.

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Copenhagen?
faq.a: Typical winter days are manageable: January averages a 37.9F high and a 33.3F low, just above the 20 to 32F caution band. Coat small, senior, and thin-coated dogs below 45F, and on rare hard freezes (the record is -17.7F) keep walks short and check paws for ice.

faq.q: How much snow should I expect on Copenhagen dog walks?
faq.a: Copenhagen averages about 21 snow days a year, concentrated December through March with nearly 6 in January. Accumulation tends to be slushy rather than deep, so the real job is rinsing road salt off paws after every winter walk.

faq.q: Are Copenhagen summers safe for dogs?
faq.a: Almost always: July averages just a 72.9F high, under the 77F caution band, so even midday walks are usually fine. In an exceptional heat wave (the record since 1768 is 96.1F), use morning harbourfront walks and fresh water stops.

cities.name: Columbus

funFacts: Columbus summers peak with July average highs of 85.4F, already past the 82F risky band for dog walks, so early morning and late evening are the safest summer walk windows.

Columbus averages 28.2 inches of snow a year, with January the snowiest month at 9.5 inches, so plan on paw wipes or booties to deal with road salt from December through February.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Columbus?
faq.a: Use caution above 77F and treat 90F as a no-go, which matters here because July average highs reach 85.4F and August stays at 84.1F. In midsummer, walk before 9 am or after sunset, and test the pavement with the back of your hand before heading out.

faq.q: Does my dog need a winter coat in Columbus?
faq.a: Small, thin-coated, and senior dogs generally need one below 45F, and Columbus spends most of the winter under that line: January averages a 37.1F high and a 22.0F low. On nights that dip toward 20F, keep walks short for every breed.

faq.q: How should I protect my dog's paws from snow and salt in Columbus?
faq.a: With 28.2 inches of snow a year and January alone averaging 9.5 inches, salted sidewalks are a fact of Columbus winters. Use booties or a paw balm before walks and rinse paws afterward so dogs do not lick off de-icing chemicals.

cities.name: Charlotte

faq.q: Does humidity really make Charlotte summers worse for dogs?

faq.q: Do dogs need winter gear in Charlotte?
faq.a: Rarely. January averages a 52.3F high and a 31.8F low, so a light sweater for small or senior dogs on frosty mornings is usually enough. With only 3.5 inches of snow a year, booties are optional, though a cold snap like the city's -5F record calls for short walks only.

cities.name: San Francisco

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in San Francisco?

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in San Francisco?
faq.a: Most dogs do not, since even January averages a 57.8F high. But winter lows sit in the mid 40s (46.6F average in January) and wind plus fog makes it feel colder, so small, lean, or senior dogs benefit from a light sweater on evening walks.

faq.q: How does the fog affect walks by neighborhood?
faq.a: Western, ocean-facing neighborhoods can run 10 or more degrees cooler than the sunny east side on a summer day, in a city where July averages only 66.3F overall. That microclimate patchwork means you can usually pick a comfortable walking route year-round, a luxury few cities offer.

cities.name: Indianapolis

faq.a: Below 45F small and senior dogs need a coat, 20 to 32F calls for caution, and below 20F is dangerous for most pets. January in Indianapolis averages a 20.9F low, so overnight and early morning winter walks should be kept to 15 minutes or less.

faq.q: Do Indianapolis dogs need booties for snow?
faq.a: It is a good idea. The city averages 25.5 inches of snow a season and January alone brings about 8.8 inches, so sidewalks stay salted for weeks. Booties or paw balm plus a post-walk rinse protect pads from both ice and de-icing chemicals.

cities.name: Seattle

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Seattle?
faq.a: Rarely by the averages, since July and August highs sit at 77.4F and 77.6F, right at the 77F caution line. The danger is heat waves like June 28, 2021, when the city hit a record 108F: Seattle dogs are not heat-acclimated, so on any day above 82F walk at dawn and skip afternoon outings.

faq.q: How should I handle Seattle's rain with a dog?
faq.a: Do not wait for a dry window that may not come: from October through March highs run 47F to 60F with frequent drizzle. A water-resistant coat for short-haired dogs, a towel at the door, and regular ear checks (damp ears invite infections) keep the routine going all winter.

faq.q: Does it get too cold or snowy for pets in Seattle?
faq.a: Not often. January lows average 37.7F, above the 20 to 32F caution band, and snowfall averages only 6.3 inches a year. When a cold snap or rare snow does arrive, shorten walks and add a coat for small or senior dogs, since local pets have little cold conditioning.

cities.name: Denver

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Denver?

faq.q: How snowy do walks get in Denver?
faq.a: Expect about 49.0 inches of snow a year, with March the snowiest month at around 8.8 inches. The good news is Denver sun melts most storms within days, but the freeze-thaw cycle leaves icy patches and salted paths, so booties or paw balm earn their keep from November through April.

faq.q: Do dogs need winter coats in Denver?
faq.a: Yes for many: January and December lows average 18.7F and 18.4F, below the 20F line where cold is dangerous for small, senior, or thin-coated dogs. Sunny winter afternoons often rebound into the 40s, so midday is the safest window for longer winter walks.

cities.name: Washington, D.C.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Washington, D.C.?
faq.a: Use caution above 77F and avoid walks at 90F or more, a threshold DC flirts with daily in July, when highs average 89.6F. Because overnight lows only fall to about 72.4F in July, even early mornings are warm, so keep summer walks short, shaded, and close to water.

faq.q: How bad is DC humidity for pets?
faq.a: Significant: panting works poorly in saturated air, so an 85.1F June day here stresses dogs more than the same temperature in a dry city. Flat-faced breeds like bulldogs and Persian cats are highest risk; give them air conditioning and limit outdoor time to minutes, not hours, in midsummer.

faq.q: Does it snow enough in DC to need dog booties?
faq.a: Occasionally. The city averages 13.7 inches a year, concentrated in January and February (February alone averages about 5.0 inches), and sidewalks get salted fast. Paw balm or booties during those weeks, plus a rinse after walks, is plenty for a typical DC winter.

cities.name: Boston

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Boston?
faq.a: Below 45F small and senior dogs need a coat, 20 to 32F calls for shortened walks, and below 20F is dangerous for most pets. Boston winters live in that caution band: January averages a 23.1F low and a 36.8F high, and harbor winds push the feels-like temperature lower still.

faq.q: How do I manage Boston snow with a dog?
faq.a: Plan for a lot of it: the city averages 49.2 inches a season, with February the peak month at 14.4 inches. Booties protect pads from ice balls and rock salt, a post-walk paw rinse prevents salt licking, and shoveled potty paths in the yard help small dogs when drifts pile up.

faq.q: Do Boston summers get too hot for dogs?
faq.a: Sometimes. July highs average 82.1F, just past the 82F risky threshold, and humid stretches can push heat stress higher. Aim for morning walks along the Charles, carry water, and skip midday fetch during heat waves; the city has reached 104F at its most extreme.

cities.name: Nashville

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Nashville?
faq.a: Above 77F use caution, above 82F it is risky, and 90F or more is dangerous; Nashville's July average high is 90.9F, so midsummer midday walks are off the table. Walk at dawn, test the pavement with your hand, and save the greenway miles for spring and fall.

faq.q: How does humidity affect Nashville dogs in summer?
faq.a: Middle Tennessee's humid air blunts panting, a dog's main cooling system, so an 87.7F June afternoon can overheat a dog faster than a drier 90F day out west. Flat-faced breeds and seniors should stay in air conditioning during afternoon heat, with potty breaks kept to a few minutes.

faq.q: Do dogs need snow gear in Nashville?
faq.a: Rarely: the city averages just 4.7 inches of snow a year, mostly in January. The bigger winter note is temperature swings, with January nights averaging 30.1F, so keep a sweater for small or senior dogs and watch for occasional ice on morning walks.

cities.name: El Paso

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in El Paso?
faq.a: For much of the warm season: highs average 97.1F in June and stay above 88F from May through September, far beyond the 90F danger line for midday walks. Walk before sunrise or after sunset, carry water, and remember desert pavement can burn paws even after the air begins to cool.

faq.q: Does the summer monsoon change dog walking in El Paso?
faq.a: Yes, mostly for the better: July and August highs ease to 95.8F and 94.0F as afternoon thunderstorms arrive, and post-storm evenings cool quickly. Watch for sudden downpours and flash-flood arroyos on trails, and never shelter under lone trees during lightning.

faq.q: Do El Paso dogs ever need cold-weather gear?
faq.a: Occasionally. January lows average 34.5F, below the 45F coat threshold for small and senior dogs, and the city picks up about 2.8 inches of snow a year, usually in December. A light coat for winter mornings covers it, though rare Arctic blasts (the record is -8F) call for indoor days.

cities.name: Detroit

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Detroit?
faq.a: January lows average 19.2F in Detroit, which is below the dangerous 20F line for extended walks. Between 20F and 32F keep outings short and purposeful, and put coats on small or senior dogs any time it is below 45F, which covers most of November through March.

faq.q: Does my dog need a winter coat in Detroit?
faq.a: For small, thin-coated, or senior dogs, yes. Average highs stay below 45F from December through February (32.3F in January), so a coat is the default for those months, and booties help with the road salt that comes with 45.0 inches of annual snow.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Detroit in summer?

cities.name: Oklahoma City

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Oklahoma City?

faq.q: What should pet owners do during Oklahoma City storm season?

cities.name: Portland

Portland averages just 4.2 inches of snow a year, so the bigger paw hazard is months of wet sidewalks: dry paws after walks to prevent irritation between the pads.

faq.a: July and August average highs of 87.8F and 88.9F, well past the 82F risky mark and close to the 90F danger line, so midday summer walks are out. Rome has recorded 105.1F, and stone streets hold heat into the evening, so wait for pavement to cool before the night walk.

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in a Roman winter?
faq.a: January lows average 38.1F, below the 45F threshold where small, senior, and short-coated dogs want a coat, while daytime highs near 53.6F are ideal for long sightseeing walks. The record low of 12.2F is rare cold for Rome.

faq.q: How rainy does Rome get for dog walks?
faq.a: Autumn is the wet season: November averages 108.2 mm and December 98.3 mm, versus just 19.8 mm in July. Plan for towel-downs and shorter loops from October to December, and enjoy the roughly 74 rainy days a year being clustered outside summer.

cities.name: Milan

Winter humidity stays near 79 to 82 percent, making damp 30s-F cold feel sharper to pets than the same temperature in a drier city.

source.name: NOAA NCEI WMO 1991-2020 climate normals (Milan Linate)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Milan?
faq.a: July averages an 87.3F high, past the 82F risky threshold, and humidity near 66 percent makes it feel worse for panting dogs. Walk at dawn or after dark in midsummer; Milan's record of 102.7F shows how brutal Po Valley heatwaves can get.

faq.q: How cold do Milan winters get for dogs?
faq.a: January lows average 31.3F, inside the 20 to 32F caution band, so put coats on small, senior, and short-haired dogs and watch for icy patches. Record cold of 3.9F is rare, but freezing fog mornings are routine.

faq.q: How do Milan's rain and fog affect dog walks?
faq.a: November is the soggiest month at 112.4 mm of rain over roughly 8.3 wet days, and autumn fog cuts visibility on evening walks. Use a reflective leash or harness and towel dogs off, since damp cold at 40F feels harsher than dry cold.

cities.name: Amsterdam

The city averages about 7.0 inches of snow a year, with February the snowiest month at roughly 2.1 inches, enough for a few magical canal-snow walks and salty-paw rinses.
January lows average 34.2F with humidity near 87 percent, damp cold that justifies coats for small, senior, and short-coated dogs below 45F.

source.name: KNMI 1991-2020 normals (Amsterdam Schiphol)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Amsterdam?
faq.a: January lows average 34.2F, so most dogs are fine with a coat for small or senior pups below 45F. Take real care in rare cold waves, since Amsterdam has dropped to -3.5F, and the 87 percent winter humidity makes freezing days feel colder.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Amsterdam?
faq.a: Rarely: July's average high is 72.5F, comfortably under the 77F caution line. During occasional heatwaves the city has reached 97.3F, and on those days switch to early-morning canal loops and shaded parks.

faq.q: How do I manage Amsterdam's constant rain with a dog?
faq.a: With about 133.2 rainy days a year and August alone averaging 98.6 mm, wet walks are unavoidable. A dog raincoat for short-haired breeds, towel-downs at the door, and drying ears well after soaked walks keep skin and coat healthy.

cities.name: Dublin

photo.alt: Rooftop view over the Dublin cityscape

funFacts: Dublin's city-centre record high is just 86.0F, one of the gentlest big-city records in Europe, so dangerous heat days for dogs are genuinely rare.
July averages a 68.2F high, squarely in the ideal range for long dog walks, making Dublin summer a walker's paradise.
Rain falls on roughly 123 days a year with at least 1 mm, peaking in November at 80.6 mm, so a good towel routine matters more than a cooling vest here.
January lows average a mild 39.4F thanks to the maritime climate, so a coat below 45F for small and senior dogs covers most of Dublin's winter needs.

source.name: Met Eireann 1991-2020 normals (Merrion Square, Dublin)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Dublin?
faq.a: Dublin winters are mild: January lows average 39.4F and highs 47.8F, so a coat for small, senior, or thin-coated dogs below 45F is usually all you need. The record low of 17.4F sits in the 20-32F caution range, so shorten walks during rare cold snaps.

faq.q: Is it ever too hot to walk a dog in Dublin?
faq.a: Almost never: July averages a 68.2F high and the city record is only 86.0F. On the handful of days above the 77F caution line, shift walks to morning and bring water, and remember flat-faced breeds struggle first.

faq.q: How should I plan around Dublin's rain with my dog?
faq.a: Expect rain on roughly 123 days a year, wettest in November at 80.6 mm. Frequent light showers mean quick towel-downs and a water-resistant coat for short-haired dogs; full washout days are less common than the reputation suggests.

cities.name: Edinburgh

photo.alt: Panorama of the Edinburgh skyline

funFacts: Edinburgh's July high averages just 66.7F, among the coolest of any major European city, so summer overheating is a rare worry for local dogs (record: 88.5F).
January lows average 35.1F, above the caution band but below the 45F coat line, so small and senior dogs wear jackets through most of the Scottish winter.
Rain arrives on about 128.3 days a year with October the wettest month at 75.7 mm, so waterproof gear beats sunscreen in this city.
December offers only 49.2 hours of sunshine all month versus 194.7 in May, so winter walks often happen in twilight: reflective collars and leads are smart kit.

source.name: Met Office 1991-2020 normals (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Edinburgh?
faq.a: January lows average 35.1F, so a coat below 45F for small, senior, and short-haired dogs handles a normal winter. Watch for cold snaps though: Edinburgh's record low is 4.1F, well inside dangerous territory, and wind chill off the Forth makes it feel colder.

faq.q: Is it ever too hot to walk a dog in Edinburgh?
faq.a: Very rarely: July averages only a 66.7F high and the all-time record is 88.5F. On the few days above the 77F caution line, walk early, carry water, and give thick-coated breeds like Huskies extra shade breaks.

faq.q: How do I handle Edinburgh's rain and dark winters with a dog?
faq.a: Rain falls on about 128.3 days a year, wettest in October at 75.7 mm, and December manages just 49.2 sunshine hours, so many walks happen in gloom. Reflective gear, a waterproof dog coat, and consistent towel-downs keep walks safe and comfortable.

cities.name: Toronto

photo.alt: Toronto skyline with the CN Tower at sunset, seen across the harbour from Snake Island

funFacts: Toronto's July afternoons average 80.6F, already past the 77F cautious walking band, so summer dog walks are safest in the early morning or after sunset.
The city averages about 47.8 inches of snow a year, and January alone brings roughly 14.6 inches, so short-coated dogs need a winter jacket and a post-walk paw wipe to clear road salt.
Sitting on the shore of Lake Ontario, Toronto gets milder winters than most of inland Canada: January highs average 31.5F, but wind off the lake can make waterfront walks feel far colder.

Toronto's all-time record high of 105F dates to July 1936, and summer humidex readings still climb into the mid 40s C, so flat-faced breeds like pugs and bulldogs should skip midday outings in a heat wave.

source.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada 1991-2020 Climate Normals (Toronto City station)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Toronto?
faq.a: January nights in Toronto average 19.9F, which sits in the dangerous band below 20F for most dogs, so keep deep-winter walks short. Small and senior dogs need a coat any time it is below 45F, and between 20F and 32F watch for shivering, lifted paws, and salt on sidewalks.

faq.q: Does my dog need boots for Toronto winters?
faq.a: It is a good idea. Toronto averages about 47.8 inches of snow a year, with measurable snow from November through April, and the city salts heavily. Boots or a paw balm plus a rinse after walks protect pads from ice balls and salt burn.

faq.q: When is it too hot for a dog walk in Toronto summer?
faq.a: July highs average 80.6F, in the risky zone above 77F, and humid spells push conditions toward the 90F danger line. On hot days walk before 9 am or after 7 pm, test pavement with the back of your hand, and give brachycephalic breeds extra indoor time.

cities.name: Vancouver

photo.alt: Downtown Vancouver skyline with the North Shore mountains behind

funFacts: Vancouver has the mildest winters of Canada's big cities: January highs average 44.2F and lows stay near 34.5F, so most dogs can walk comfortably all winter with little more than a light coat.
Snow is a bit part here, only about 14.4 inches a year on average, but the rainy season from November to March means a dog raincoat and a towel by the door earn their keep.
Summers are made for dogs: July highs average just 72.3F, below the 77F caution line, so midday walks are usually safe even in peak summer.

Wedged between the Pacific and the North Shore mountains, Vancouver's record high at the airport is only 94F, set July 30, 2009, though rare heat events mean owners should still know the 82F risky and 90F danger thresholds.

source.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada 1991-2020 Climate Normals (Vancouver International Airport)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Vancouver?
faq.a: Rarely too cold: January lows average 34.5F, above the 20F to 32F caution band, so most healthy dogs walk year round. Small, senior, or short-coated dogs still benefit from a coat below 45F, which covers most December through February mornings.

faq.q: How do I keep my dog comfortable in Vancouver's rainy season?
faq.a: From November through March highs sit between 44.2F and 50.2F with frequent rain, a combination that chills wet dogs quickly. A waterproof coat for thin-coated breeds, towel-drying after walks, and checking paws for grit keep the wet season pleasant.

faq.q: Does it snow enough in Vancouver to worry about my dog's paws?
faq.a: Occasionally. Vancouver averages only 14.4 inches of snow a year, mostly in December and January, but when it falls the city applies salt that can irritate pads. Rinse paws after snowy walks and keep sessions short when temperatures drop below freezing.

cities.name: Montreal

January highs average just 23F and overnight lows sink to 7.7F, well below the 20F danger line, so deep-winter dog walks should be short, brisk, and coat-equipped.
Summers swing the other way: July highs average 80.1F with humidity off the St. Lawrence River, and the record high of 100F was set on August 1, 1975, so hot-weather walk timing matters here too.

Montreal is an island city in the St. Lawrence River, and its riverside parks are breezy in summer but brutally wind-chilled in winter, when the wind can make 7.7F nights feel far colder on exposed paths.

source.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada 1991-2020 Climate Normals (Montreal-Trudeau International Airport)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Montreal?
faq.a: Treat much of January and February as hazardous: average lows of 7.7F in January are well below the 20F danger threshold, so limit walks to quick relief breaks with a coat and booties. Between 20F and 32F, common in December and March, keep walks under 30 minutes for most breeds.

faq.q: How much snow should I plan for with my dog in Montreal?
faq.a: A lot: about 85.3 inches a year on average, with snow cover typical from December through March and January averaging 20.5 inches alone. Plan for booties or paw balm against heavy salting, and expect indoor enrichment days during major storms.

faq.q: Do Montreal summers get too hot for dogs?
faq.a: Yes, regularly. July highs average 80.1F, above the 77F caution line, and humid heat waves have reached a record 100F. Walk early or late on hot days, carry water, and remember humidity makes any reading feel worse for dogs.

cities.name: Calgary

Calgary averages 54.6 inches of snow a year and has recorded measurable snow in every month except July and August, with March the snowiest month at about 9.4 inches.
At roughly 1,084 m elevation, Calgary keeps its summer nights cool: even July lows average 50.4F, so early morning walks are comfortable all summer long.
The city's record low of -49F was set on February 4, 1893, and modern January nights still average 7.7F, firmly in the danger zone where walks should be short and coats mandatory.

source.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada 1991-2020 Climate Normals (Calgary International Airport)

faq.q: How cold is too cold to walk a dog in Calgary?
faq.a: January and December lows average 7.7F and 10.2F, below the 20F danger line, so midwinter walks should be brief relief breaks with coats and booties. When chinook winds lift afternoons above freezing, seize the window for a proper outing.

faq.q: Can it really snow in Calgary outside of winter?
faq.a: Yes. Calgary averages 54.6 inches of snow a year and normals show measurable snow in every month except July and August, including about 9 inches in April. Keep a paw towel handy well into spring and do not pack the dog coat away before May.

faq.q: Do Calgary summers get too hot for dogs?
faq.a: Occasionally. July highs average a pleasant 74.3F, but the record high of 98F (August 10, 2018) shows heat waves happen. Above 77F be cautious, above 82F keep walks short and shaded, and cool mornings near 50.4F make dawn the reliable choice.

cities.name: Mexico City

The all-time record high is only 94F, set May 25, 2024, but thin high-altitude air means intense sun: shade breaks and water matter even when the thermometer looks tame.

source.name: Servicio Meteorologico Nacional 1991-2020 climate normals (Tacubaya observatory)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Mexico City?
faq.a: The hot window is late spring: April highs average 81.5F, close to the 82F risky line, so walk before 10 am or after 6 pm in April and May. High-altitude sun is strong, so add shade and water even on days that read below 77F.

faq.q: Do dogs need a coat in Mexico City?
faq.a: Sometimes. December and January lows average around 47.3F to 48.2F, and cold snaps have hit a record 24F, so small, senior, or short-coated dogs benefit from a sweater on early morning winter walks. Midday winter highs near 72F are usually coat-free.

faq.q: How does the rainy season affect dog walks in Mexico City?
faq.a: From June through September, afternoons often bring heavy showers while mornings stay dry, and highs ease to about 75F to 78F. Schedule the main walk before midday, dry paws after wet outings, and keep indoor games ready for stormy afternoons.

cities.name: São Paulo

Famous for its fine drizzle, the 'terra da garoa' gets frequent light rain, so a quick towel-dry after walks helps prevent damp-coat chills in the 55F winter nights.

source.name: INMET 1991-2020 climate normals (Mirante de Santana station)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in São Paulo?
faq.a: From December through February, highs average 84.2F in February, above the 82F risky threshold, and humidity pushes the felt heat higher. Walk before 9 am or after sunset in summer, and treat any 90F day, like the record 101F of October 17, 2014, as an indoor day.

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in São Paulo's winter?
faq.a: Usually not, but keep one handy for small or senior dogs. July lows average 55F, above the 45F coat threshold, though cold fronts can drop nights toward the station record of 28F, when a sweater for thin-coated breeds is sensible.

faq.q: How should I plan walks around São Paulo's rain?
faq.a: Summer (December to February) brings frequent afternoon storms alongside 84F heat, while winters are drier. Aim for morning walks year round: you dodge both the summer downpours and the worst heat, and dry your dog's coat after the city's famous drizzle.

cities.name: Buenos Aires

funFacts: January in Buenos Aires averages highs of 86.2F, well past the 82F risky band for dog walks, so porteno dogs do their summer strolling at dawn or after dark.

Winters are gentle: July highs average 59.9F with lows of 45.5F, right at the 45F coat threshold, so most dogs need only a light sweater on the chilliest mornings.

Sitting on the humid estuary of the Rio de la Plata, Buenos Aires pairs its heat with sticky humidity, which makes an 86F afternoon feel far hotter to a panting dog than the same reading in a dry climate.

source.name: Servicio Meteorologico Nacional (Argentina) 1991-2020 climate normals (Buenos Aires Central Observatory)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Buenos Aires?
faq.a: December through February is the danger window: January highs average 86.2F, above the 82F risky line, and humidity makes it feel worse. Walk before 9 am or after 8 pm in summer, and on heat-wave days approaching the record 110F keep dogs indoors with water and fans.

faq.q: Do dogs need coats in a Buenos Aires winter?
faq.a: Only the vulnerable ones. July lows average 45.5F, right at the 45F threshold where small, senior, and short-coated dogs benefit from a coat, while July highs near 60F make midday walks comfortable for everyone. The record low is 22F, but frosts like that are rare.

faq.q: How does humidity affect dog walks in Buenos Aires?
faq.a: The Rio de la Plata keeps the city humid year round, and humidity impairs a dog's panting-based cooling. That means a January afternoon of 86.2F can stress a dog as much as a hotter dry day, so shorten summer walks, favor shade, and carry water.

cities.name: Sydney

funFacts: Sydney's January highs average 80.6F, already in the cautious band above 77F, and coastal humidity means beach-adjacent morning walks beat baking afternoon pavement.

Winters are a dog's dream: July highs average 64.2F with lows of 48F, so midday winter walks need no coat for most breeds and the 45F coat threshold is rarely crossed.
June is Sydney's wettest month, averaging 142 mm of rain as east coast lows roll in, so keep a towel by the door and a backup indoor game plan for autumn and early winter.

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Sydney?
faq.a: In summer, December through February, highs average 80.6F in January, above the 77F caution line, and humid days push the felt heat higher. Walk before 9 am or after 6 pm, and on westerly heat-wave days heading toward the record 114F, skip outdoor exercise entirely.

faq.q: Does my dog need a winter coat in Sydney?
faq.a: Most do not. July highs average 64.2F and lows sit around 48F, just above the 45F threshold where small and senior dogs want a coat. Only on the coldest mornings, with the record low at 36F, should thin-coated breeds get a light layer.

faq.q: What about rain and storms on Sydney dog walks?
faq.a: June is the wettest month at 142 mm on average, and summer can bring sudden southerly busters with gusty storms. Check the radar before long walks in autumn and early winter, dry your dog after wet outings, and note that mild 64F winter days make rainy-week catch-up walks easy.

cities.name: Melbourne

photo.alt: Princes Bridge over the Yarra River with the Melbourne skyline

funFacts: Melbourne is famous for four seasons in one day: January highs average 80.6F, yet cold fronts off Bass Strait can drop temperatures 20 degrees in an afternoon, so pack for both ends of a dog walk.
The city's record high of 116F came on February 7, 2009, during the Black Saturday heat wave, a reminder that Melbourne summers can turn from mild to dangerous for pets in a single day.
Winter walks are brisk but safe: July highs average 56.1F with lows of 42.4F, just under the 45F line where small and senior dogs appreciate a coat.
Snow is essentially unknown in the city itself, and the record low is 27F (July 21, 1869), so a light winter jacket covers even a Melbourne dog's coldest mornings.

source.name: Bureau of Meteorology 1991-2020 climate normals (Melbourne Airport)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Melbourne?
faq.a: January and February highs average 80.6F and 80.1F, in the caution zone above 77F, but the real hazard is heat-wave days: the record is 116F, set February 7, 2009. On any forecast above 90F keep dogs indoors, and in normal summer weather walk early morning or evening.

faq.q: Does my dog need a coat in Melbourne's winter?
faq.a: Small, senior, and short-coated dogs often do. July lows average 42.4F, just below the 45F coat threshold, though midday highs of 56.1F are comfortable for most breeds. Time the main walk for early afternoon in winter and save sweaters for morning outings.

faq.q: How do I handle Melbourne's famously changeable weather with a dog?
faq.a: Expect swings: a summer day can open at 80F and finish 20 degrees cooler after a southerly change. Check the hourly forecast before long walks, carry water when it is above 77F, and keep a towel ready, since fast-moving fronts often bring brief heavy showers.

cities.name: Brisbane

funFacts: Brisbane's subtropical summer is serious for dogs: January highs average 86.7F, past the 82F risky line, and coastal humidity means dawn walks are the default from November to March.
Winter is the payoff: July highs average 71.6F with lows of 50.9F, so even midday winter walks sit comfortably below the 77F caution threshold.
The record high of 107F was set on February 22, 2004, and hot pavement lingers into the evening here, so the back-of-hand pavement test matters even after sunset in a heat wave.
Brisbane has never had city snow, and its record low at the current station is a gentle 37F, so most local dogs will never need more than a token winter sweater.

source.name: Bureau of Meteorology 1999-2024 climate normals (Brisbane station)

faq.q: When is it too hot to walk a dog in Brisbane?
faq.a: Most of summer: January highs average 86.7F, above the 82F risky line, and humid nights that only fall to 71.1F limit evening relief. From November through March, walk at dawn, keep sessions short, and treat 90F-plus days, up to the record 107F, as indoor days.

faq.q: Does my dog ever need a coat in Brisbane?
faq.a: Rarely. July lows average 50.9F, above the 45F coat threshold, and winter highs of 71.6F are ideal walking weather. Only on unusual cold snaps near the station record of 37F would a small or senior dog want a light layer for early morning outings.

faq.q: How do Brisbane's summer storms affect dog walks?
faq.a: Summer combines 86.7F average January heat with frequent afternoon thunderstorms, so the morning walk is doubly important. Keep anxious dogs indoors when storms build, and after rain remember humid 80F-plus air still stresses dogs even though the pavement has cooled.
